<teammate-message teammate_id="chirp-android-platform" color="cyan" summary="Android platform migration PR open, live-render gap filed">
PR: https://github.com/pablof7z/chirp/pull/41 ("Closes #35 (Android portion), Closes #36 (Android portion)"), branch chirp-android-platform, pushed.

chirp#35 (Android): regenerated the stale nmp.nip01.* Kotlin FlatBuffers types as nmp.note_feed.* (schema id nmp.note_feed.opfeed, file id NNFS, v2, card NoteFeedItem) from the pinned NMP schema (crates/nmp-note-feed/schema/op_feed.fbs @ fa49d00c5). Rewrote TypedHomeFeedDecoder.kt and the Chirp*/ model types for the new shape — relation_counts/author_display_name/author_picture_url/content_preview are gone from the wire (dropped for good, not a bug: display data is now component-owned via LocalNostrProfileHost, which TimelineScreen.kt already had a fallback path for), hosted_group is new and wired through. Updated NoteActions.kt so the Reply/React/Repost/Zap buttons work without a counts payload (counts absent is expected per your note, not regressed). Golden-fixture tests (OpFeedDecoderTest, TypedHomeFeedDecoderContractTest) rewritten against nmp-note-feed's real v2 hex fixtures — 19/19 passing. Added apps/android/scripts/regen-flatbuffers.sh closing the no-regen-script gap — and it caught a real landmine: `brew install flatbuffers` installs 25.12.19, but the checked-in Kotlin runtime is pinned to 25.2.10; the wrong flatc silently emits code calling a Constants method that doesn't exist in the pinned runtime. Script now hard-requires the exact version (downloads a matching release binary, doesn't rely on brew).
 [...] <teammate-message teammate_id="feed-empty-diagnosis" color="red" summary="No schema mismatch — it's projection_rev (NMP #2952). Chirp guards PR #44.">
Both done — but with an important correction: there is NO schema/key mismatch. I inspected both host decoders at chirp master (post #38/#41) and they already match the emitted descriptor exactly.

## (b) Result: NOT a schema/key mismatch — it's the projection_rev contract
- Android `TypedHomeFeedDecoder.kt`: `PROJECTION_KEY="chirp.timeline.home"`, `SCHEMA_ID="nmp.note_feed.opfeed"`, `FILE_IDENTIFIER="NNFS"`; it even documents the retired `NOFS`/`nmp.nip01.opfeed` v1 as gone (chirp#35 done).
- iOS `TypedHomeFeedDecoder.swift`: identical — `projectionKey="chirp.timeline.home"`, `schemaId="nmp.note_feed.opfeed"`, `fileIdentifier="NNFS"`.
Both gate on `key == PROJECTION_KEY && schemaId == SCHEMA_ID` with the correct values. chirp#35's migration is correct; nothing to fix there.

The golden-pass/live-fail signature you flagged is NOT a schema mismatch — it's the rev-guard: the golden fixture tests call `TypedHomeFeedDecoder.decode(bytes)` DIRECTLY, bypassing the rev-aware `ProjectionMergeCache`; and `ProjectionCacheTest` only ever used advancing revs. The LIVE path (`KernelModel.decodeUpdate`) runs `projectionCache.merge()` FIRST, which skips a Changed row when `incomingRev <= cached.rev`. The app-owned home key emitted `projection_rev=0` every tick (the NMP bug I already fixed in #2952), so the cache committed the first empty frame and skipped every later card frame → "decodedRev advances but 0 cards." Note the host `ProjectionCache.kt`/`.swift` are BOTH generated ("DO NOT EDIT BY HAND", from NMP codegen) — so there's no hand-editable host mismatch anyway, and they're correct given a contract-compliant rev.

So the fix is NMP #2952 (emit content-advancing projection_rev for app-owned keys) — one wire-contract fix, iOS+Android+web corrected at once, no host-decode change. I did NOT fabricate a Chirp schema fix for a non-bug.
